# Add immutable per-group transaction history and cursor

## Context

D#18224 measured `data.Store` versus `collection.Base` at depth 50 over the real Workstation document: latency differed only 1.04x, while mutability was decisive. Store insertion writes an internal id and Models expose replacement setters; frozen plain rows in a Collection can be the append-only authority.

## The Problem

There is no user-facing dock history. Adding a mutable Store as authority would permit whole-field replacement of retained transactions, while statically importing it would make single-window/history-disabled apps pay for unused machinery. Cursor, redo invalidation, eviction, and retirement are Group-local invariants, not global filters.

## The Architectural Reality

A Group owns one bounded history and cursor. The authoritative vehicle is a `collection.Base` of recursively frozen plain records. A `data.Store` may be created lazily as a read-only projection for grids/Neural Link inspection, but it never drives adoption or cursor decisions. A Group-level Provider publishes derived command state.

## The Fix

Implement generic History/Group cursor semantics: append, undo, redo, redo-tail invalidation, depth eviction, immutable serialization, and provider projections. Dynamically load the history module at the first admitted transaction; the load is an admission barrier and queues the original descriptor exactly once. `historyDepth: 0` imports nothing.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| authoritative history | D#18224 H2 | frozen plain rows in `collection.Base` | disabled at depth 0 | JSDoc | nested + whole-field mutation controls |
| cursor | D#18224 criteria 7/8 | Group-local undo/redo/append/preserve | bounds fail closed | JSDoc | branch/eviction unit matrix |
| Provider state | explicit cross-window Provider parent | `canUndo`, `canRedo`, depth/status | false/empty before load | guide/JSDoc | multi-window binding arm |
| optional Store view | manager.Store precedent | lazy read-only clones | destroy/rebuild loses no truth | JSDoc | mutation cannot affect authority |
| module admission | D#18224 criterion 13 | await once before mutation; enqueue once | load failure leaves no mutation | JSDoc | red control at first gesture |

## Decision Record impact

Depends on amended ADR 0029; no new ADR.

## Decision Record

Required prerequisite: the #18303 hard-cut authority leaf.

## Discussion Criteria Mapping

Owns criteria 1–3's H2 vehicle, single-window cost, bounded history, and cursor half of criterion 7.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] History rows are recursively frozen after Collection admission and reject nested mutation and whole-field replacement.
- [ ] Append after undo drops only the redo tail; depth eviction and cursor bounds are Group-local and deterministic.
- [ ] Frozen bytes emitted for a retained row remain unchanged after every rejected mutation control.
- [ ] `historyDepth: 0` causes zero static/dynamic history-module loads and leaves single-window behavior byte-equivalent.
- [ ] The first enabled transaction awaits one dynamic import before participant mutation and enqueues its original descriptor exactly once.
- [ ] The Group Provider exposes correct `canUndo` / `canRedo` in every bound window without presentation sweeps.
- [ ] Any TransactionStore is lazy, read-only, clone-fed, and disposable without changing authority.

## Out of Scope

Participant adoption, native effects, persisted topology snapshots, or Neural Link command migration.

## Avoided Traps

No mutable Model authority; no global Store filtered by Group; no eager import; no second cursor in a UI projection.
